questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The courses available at McGill

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Slightly complicated but easy to find with help from someone local

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Help from co-students and professors regarding access to courses

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very easy, i found it through Facebook but i did have to move apartments after 2 months

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Distance to campus and transportation

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: there is a cost of living crisis in Montreal and that effects everyone. My housing was not student specific so i wouldn't know.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was a lot of issues regarding access to courses because of prerequisites - which was all solvable by communicating with the professors but still was a bit anxiety inducing with securing spots on courses etc.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
Im guessing that this is regarding registering for courses? i find the question quite unclear. 
After being accepted i received and account for McGills intranet where you managed everything regarding courses and registrations. It was first come first served regarding courses - a lot of courses were already full before exchange students got access to register which was a bit of a stumble to find courses that were useful and available

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: professors were very helpfull but also McGill IT department etc.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: In the end I got into the classes i wanted though a lot of the ones i originally wanted were not available for the fall semester which was not available information anywhere until i got there

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure you have options for courses and not dependent on only a list of four most likely some will be full or unavailable.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was very satisifed with the courses and theoretic content though the academic practice was immensely different from what I am used to. It less about doing research and mostly about reiterating theory that is not applying it in practice. Also the courses are based more on smaller assignments and essays.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: i took both 200 and 300 level courses. Depending on the specific course i found the levels extremely fluctuating from course to course.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I mostly had lecture based classes over classroom classes which was a big change from UCPH. Also as mentioned the work is more spread out over the semester instead of compressed into one exam.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
COMS 350 Sound Culture
COMS 310 Media and Feminist Studies
GSFS 250 Sexual and Gender Diversity Studies
ANTH 202 Socio-Cultural Anthropology

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Any course that have specific targets, the variety of subjects is wider than at UCPH and is a great oppurtunity to learn about more niche and specific fields.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A bunch of things though I didn't attend any

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: There is a lot of film showings and the like that i would recommend

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Wander around the city, go on hikes and cabin trips!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy, easier than i thought.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I didnt manage to get many friends from my uni and mostly met friends through my roommates.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The academic practice at the university was challenging to adjust to, especially within the student group.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness and laid back attitude of the locals!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Go in the fall to avoid the heavy winter and go early so you have the summer!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure to talk with and use the advice of your professors, go to office hours etc! I wish i had taken more advantage of having professors who were so engaged with their students.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The academic inspiration and the friends i made.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Keeping track of all the practicalities

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
